Is the conjugacy problem decidable for every one-relator group
$\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n \mid r\rangle$?

More precisely, after fixing any finite set of generators and any single
relator $r$, is there an algorithm which decides, for each pair of words over

conjugate in the group presented by $r$? The algorithm may depend on the fixed
presentation.

          (PresentedGroup.mk {FreeGroup.mk r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.34»
modeling_decisions: Words are represented by Mathlib's standard signed-word syntax `List (Fin n × Bool)` and interpreted by `FreeGroup.mk`; this gives a primitive recursive input coding while covering every free-group word.
The one-relator group is `PresentedGroup {FreeGroup.mk r}`, so the singleton relation set is quotiented by its normal closure exactly as in a group presentation.
The quantifier order `∀ n r, ComputablePred ...` expresses the specified non-uniform reading: after each finite presentation is fixed, its conjugacy predicate on pairs of words is computable.

The theorem includes `n = 0` and trivial relator words. These degenerate finite presentations yield the trivial group and do not change the intended universal question; a reviewer may confirm whether an explicit positivity/nontrivial-relator convention is desired.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.34

by D. I. Moldavanskiĭ

(Well-known problem). The conjugacy problem for groups with a single defining relation.

A group with a single defining relation (a one-relator group) is a group
$G = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r \rangle$ given by finitely many generators and one
defining relator $r$, a word in the generators and their inverses. The conjugacy problem
for $G$ asks for an algorithm which, given two words $u, v$ in the generators and their
inverses, decides whether the elements of $G$ they represent are conjugate in $G$.
The problem asks whether the conjugacy problem is solvable for every such group.

Words in the generators $x_1, \dots, x_n$ and their inverses are modelled as lists
`List (Fin n × Bool)`, the group as `PresentedGroup {r}` with `r : FreeGroup (Fin n)`,
and solvability of the conjugacy problem as computability (in the sense of
`ComputablePred`) of the predicate "the two words represent conjugate elements". The
quantifier is non-uniform: for each one-relator group there should exist an algorithm.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.34»

/--
(Well-known problem). Is the conjugacy problem solvable for every group with a single
defining relation? That is, for every one-relator group
$G = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r \rangle$, is there an algorithm deciding, for any two
words $u, v$ in the generators and their inverses, whether $u$ and $v$ represent conjugate
elements of $G$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.34» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin n)),
      ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.1))
          (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.34»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table's reading (non-uniform decidability for every finitely generated one-relator group, no variants for partial results such as Newman's torsion case) is the standard interpretation and was followed exactly.
modeling_decisions: Generating set is taken to be `Fin n` for some `n : ℕ` (finitely generated, as the notes prescribe); any finite generating set is isomorphic to this and `Fin n` carries a `Primcodable` instance.

The single relator is an element `r : FreeGroup (Fin n)` rather than a word `List (Fin n × Bool)`; since the quantifier is non-uniform (∃ algorithm per group), this choice does not change the statement.

Inputs to the algorithm are pairs of (not necessarily reduced) words `List (Fin n × Bool)` over the generators and their inverses, mapped to the group via `FreeGroup.mk` then `PresentedGroup.mk {r}`; this matches 'pairs of words over the generators representing conjugate elements'.
Decidability is Mathlib's `ComputablePred` (∃ DecidablePred instance with computable `decide`), i.e. a non-uniform algorithm for each fixed one-relator group, per the decomposition notes.
Degenerate presentations are included: `n = 0` (trivial group) and `r = 1` (free group) are one-relator groups with solvable conjugacy problem, so their inclusion does not affect the truth value.
`answer(True)` means the conjugacy problem is solvable for every one-relator group; `answer(False)` means some one-relator group has unsolvable conjugacy problem.

kourovka.«3.34».why: Stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin n)), ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool) => IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.1)) (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2))`. One-relator group = `PresentedGroup {r}` on finitely many generators `Fin n`; words over generators and inverses = `List (Fin n × Bool)`; conjugacy = Mathlib `IsConj` (checked to unfold to ∃ c, c u c⁻¹ = v in the group); solvability = Mathlib `ComputablePred`, which is non-uniform (one algorithm per fixed presentation), as the decomposition notes require. Only existing Mathlib primitives are used.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.34

by D. I. Moldavanskiĭ

(Well-known problem). The conjugacy problem for groups with a single defining
relation.

That is: is the conjugacy problem solvable for every one-relator group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r \rangle$? For such a group, the conjugacy problem
asks for an algorithm that decides, given two words $u, v$ in the generators
$x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}$, whether $u$ and $v$ represent conjugate
elements of the group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.34»

/--
The conjugacy problem for the presented group $\langle \alpha \mid \text{rels} \rangle$
is solvable: the set of pairs of words $(u, v)$ over the alphabet
$\alpha \sqcup \alpha^{-1}$ (encoded as `List (α × Bool)`) such that $u$ and $v$
represent conjugate elements of `PresentedGroup rels` is a computable predicate.
-/
def HasSolvableConjugacyProblem {α : Type*} [Primcodable α] (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun p : List (α × Bool) × List (α × Bool) =>
    IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk p.1)) (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk p.2))

/--
Is the conjugacy problem solvable for every group with a single defining relation,
i.e. for every group $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r \rangle$ with finitely many
generators and one relator $r$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.34» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin n)), HasSolvableConjugacyProblem {r} := by
  sorry

/-- With no generators, every one-relator group is trivial, so its conjugacy problem is
solvable. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem hasSolvableConjugacyProblem_fin_zero (r : FreeGroup (Fin 0)) :
    HasSolvableConjugacyProblem {r} := by
  have h : ∀ p : List (Fin 0 × Bool) × List (Fin 0 × Bool),
      IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.1))
        (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) := by
    intro p
    have : FreeGroup.mk p.1 = FreeGroup.mk p.2 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    rw [this]
  exact ⟨fun p => isTrue (h p), by simpa using Computable.const true⟩

end Kourovka.«3.34»

by D. I. Moldavanskiĭ

The conjugacy problem for groups with a single defining relation.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.34»

/--
Is the conjugacy problem decidable for every group with a finite set of generators and a single
defining relator? More precisely, for every $n$ and every relator $r$, is the predicate on pairs of
words $u,v$ that asserts that their images are conjugate in
$\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n \mid r\rangle$ computable?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.34» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : List (Fin n × Bool)),
      ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        IsConj
          (PresentedGroup.mk ({FreeGroup.mk r} : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk p.1))
          (PresentedGroup.mk ({FreeGroup.mk r} : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.34»
modeling_decisions: Represented a word over n generators by `List (Fin n × Bool)`, Mathlib's raw-word representation underlying `FreeGroup`; this keeps the inputs `Primcodable`.
Represented the one-relator group ⟨x₁,…,xₙ | r⟩ as `PresentedGroup {FreeGroup.mk r}`, whose defining quotient is by the normal closure of the singleton relator.
Used Mathlib's recursion-theoretic `ComputablePred`, rather than plain `DecidablePred`, to express algorithmic decidability.
Placed `n` and `r` under the universal quantifier outside `ComputablePred`, expressing the requested non-uniform algorithm for each fixed finite presentation.
Allowed `n = 0`; this is the natural boundary case of a finite generator type `Fin n` and only adds the trivial zero-generator presentation.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.34

by D. I. Moldavanskiĭ

(Well-known problem). The conjugacy problem for groups with a single defining relation.

That is: is the conjugacy problem solvable for every one-relator group
$G = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r \rangle$? In other words, for each such group, is there
an algorithm which, given two words $u, v$ in the letters $x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}$,
decides whether the elements of $G$ represented by $u$ and $v$ are conjugate in $G$?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.34»

/--
(Well-known problem). The conjugacy problem for groups with a single defining relation.

Is the conjugacy problem solvable for every group with a single defining relation? That is,
for every $n$ and every element $r$ of the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$, letting
$G = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r \rangle$, is the predicate on pairs $(u, v)$ of words over
the alphabet $x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}$ which holds exactly when the images of $u$ and $v$
in $G$ are conjugate a computable predicate?

A word is a `List (Fin n × Bool)`, as in `FreeGroup.mk`: the letter `(i, true)` is $x_i$ and
`(i, false)` is $x_i^{-1}$. The decision procedure may depend on $n$ and $r$, i.e. the question
is asked for each one-relator group separately.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.34» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin n)),
      ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.1))
          (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check of the formulation in the degenerate case of no generators: the group
$\langle \; \mid r \rangle$ is trivial, so any two words represent conjugate elements, and the
conjugacy predicate is computable.
-/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem computablePred_isConj_of_fin_zero (r : FreeGroup (Fin 0)) :
    ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin 0 × Bool) × List (Fin 0 × Bool) =>
      IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.1))
        (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) := by
  have h : ∀ x : PresentedGroup ({r} : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0))), x = 1 := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _ x
    rw [Subsingleton.elim y 1, map_one]
  have this : ∀ p : List (Fin 0 × Bool) × List (Fin 0 × Bool),
      IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.1))
        (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2)) := fun p => by
    rw [h (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.1)), h (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2))]
  refine ⟨fun p => .isTrue (this p), ?_⟩
  simpa [this] using Computable.const true

end Kourovka.«3.34»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot reading (non-uniform decidability of the conjugacy problem for each finitely generated one-relator group) is the standard interpretation of this well-known problem, and the file conforms to it.
modeling_decisions: Generators are indexed by `Fin n` for an arbitrary `n : ℕ` (implicitly finite generating set, as in the decomposition notes); every finitely generated one-relator group is isomorphic to one of this form.

Words are modelled as `List (Fin n × Bool)` (the raw word type of `FreeGroup.mk`, letter `(i, true)` = x_i, `(i, false)` = x_i⁻¹) rather than as elements of `FreeGroup (Fin n)`, because `ComputablePred` needs a `Primcodable` domain and Mathlib has no `Primcodable (FreeGroup α)` instance; lists over `Fin n × Bool` have the standard instance. This matches the informal 'pairs of words over the generators'.

The relator `r` ranges over all of `FreeGroup (Fin n)`, including `r = 1` (free group) and `n = 0` (trivial group); these degenerate presentations have decidable conjugacy problems, so including them does not change the truth value of the question. A `category test` theorem checks the `n = 0` case.
Conjugacy is `IsConj` in `PresentedGroup {r}`; for a group this is ordinary conjugacy (∃ c, c * a * c⁻¹ = b).
The decidability notion is Mathlib's `ComputablePred` (partial recursive functions on ℕ via `Primcodable` encodings), which is the standard formal counterpart of 'the conjugacy problem is solvable'.
AMS tags `3 20`: computability (03D40, word/conjugacy problems) and group theory (20F10).

kourovka.«3.34».why: Stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin n)), ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool) => IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.1)) (PresentedGroup.mk {r} (FreeGroup.mk p.2))`. This is the standard yes/no reading: for every finitely generated one-relator group ⟨x_1,…,x_n | r⟩, the set of pairs of words over the generators x_i^{±1} that represent conjugate elements is a computable predicate (Mathlib's `ComputablePred`, i.e. decidable in the standard model of computation). The quantifier is non-uniform (the algorithm may depend on n and r), as the decomposition notes require. All primitives are from Mathlib: `ComputablePred`, `PresentedGroup.mk`, `FreeGroup.mk`, `IsConj`, and the `Primcodable` instance on `List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool)`.
